title: Kings That Do Not Touch

concept.title: For every square: leave it empty, or put a king if no neighbour has one
body: A king attacks the eight squares around it (also the diagonals). Count the ways to place `k` kings on an `n` by `n` board so that **no two kings are neighbours** (no two kings touch, even at a corner). Go through the squares in reading order. For each square there are two choices: leave it empty, or put a king there. A king is allowed only if none of the kings placed before is within one row and one column of it.

body.code:
def place(pos, k):                       # k kings are still to be placed
    if k == 0:
        return 1
    if pos == n * n or n * n - pos < k:
        return 0                          # not enough squares left
    row, col = divmod(pos, n)
    total = place(pos + 1, k)             # leave this square empty
    if all(abs(row - r2) > 1 or abs(col - c2) > 1 for r2, c2 in placed):
        placed.append((row, col))
        total += place(pos + 1, k - 1)
        placed.pop()
    return total

body: The check `n * n - pos < k` stops a branch that can no longer place all the kings: with few squares left there is no hope. Pruning of this kind ("not enough room left") is common in problems where you must choose exactly `k` objects. Squares where a king would touch an earlier king are skipped.

statement: Count the ways to place exactly `k` kings on an `n` by `n` chessboard so that no two kings attack each other, that is, no two kings are in squares that share a side or a corner. Two placements are different if the sets of squares are different.
outputFormat: Print the number of placements (it can be 0).

examples.note: There are C(9, 2) = 36 pairs of squares and 20 of them touch, so 16 placements remain.

hints: Handle the squares in reading order and decide: empty, or a king.
A king may be placed if no earlier king is within one row and one column.
Stop a branch when there are fewer squares left than kings still to place.

explanation: Squares are taken in reading order: leave empty, or place a king when no earlier king is within one row and one column. A branch ends with 1 when all `k` kings are placed and with 0 when too few squares remain.
solution.complexity: Time proportional to the number of partial placements (at most about 16 000 for n = 5), space O(k).

code.python:
def place(n, pos, k, placed):
    if k == 0:
        return 1
    if pos == n * n or n * n - pos < k:
        return 0
    row, col = divmod(pos, n)
    total = place(n, pos + 1, k, placed)
    if all(abs(row - r2) > 1 or abs(col - c2) > 1 for r2, c2 in placed):
        placed.append((row, col))
        total += place(n, pos + 1, k - 1, placed)
        placed.pop()
    return total

n, k = map(int, input().split())

print(place(n, 0, k, []))
